stem: Which sequence gives the increasing order of boiling points of the Group 15 hydrides?

verdicts.working: Boiling points are approximately PH₃ −88°C, AsH₃ −63°C, NH₃ −33°C, and SbH₃ −17°C. Thus PH₃ < AsH₃ < NH₃ < SbH₃.

working:
$\text{PH}_3 < \text{AsH}_3$ in boiling point as dispersion forces increase with molar mass.
$\text{NH}_3$ has hydrogen bonding, so its boiling point exceeds that of $\text{AsH}_3$.
$\text{SbH}_3$ has the greatest molar mass and strongest dispersion forces, giving the highest boiling point.

Independent check: Boiling points are approximately PH₃ −88°C, AsH₃ −63°C, NH₃ −33°C, and SbH₃ −17°C. Thus PH₃ < AsH₃ < NH₃ < SbH₃.
solution:
Down Group 15, increasing molar mass strengthens dispersion forces, so $\text{PH}_3 < \text{AsH}_3 < \text{SbH}_3$. Hydrogen bonding raises the boiling point of $\text{NH}_3$ above $\text{AsH}_3$, while $\text{SbH}_3$ remains highest.
$$\text{PH}_3 < \text{AsH}_3 < \text{NH}_3 < \text{SbH}_3$$
